messages:
maya: heads-up — after the kernel-selection pass yesterday I started seeing higher p99 token latencies and two co-residency OOMs on prod-gpu-3. digging in now. anyone else see this?

liam: saw one OOM earlier. looked like kv cache was evicting aggressively when a small model got packed next to a large one. memory pressure spikes during kernel fallback path?

sophia: can you paste the logs? was it during batching spike or steady load?

maya: logs attached below. happened under steady 40rps multimodel mix (gpt-small + med + embedder). profiler shows kernel fallback for attention at ~t=1723456820 and simultaneous slab compaction.

maya: ```
2024-03-12T14:07:12Z WARN runtime::kernel "fallback to generic" model=gpt-med seq=1024 ctx=8
2024-03-12T14:07:12Z INFO allocator "slab_compact" reclaimed=256MB free=3.2GB
2024-03-12T14:07:12Z ERROR oom::alloc "failed to reserve workspace" model=gpt-small needed=120MB free_after_compact=48MB
```

chen: looks like two things aligning: kernel selection moved some ops to the slower generic kernel which increases transient workspace usage; and our per-model soft-quota for KV cache is being bumped when model swap happens. the allocator then compacts which fragments and fails the small allocation.

aj: we already had heuristics for swap prefetch (kv_prefetch_window) but it assumes constant kernel memory. if fallback increases temp buffers we under-provision.

liam: proposal: run an experiment with guarded workspace headroom + adaptive kv-credit throttling. i.e. reserve an extra 10% workspace for fallback paths and reduce kv-credit for lower-priority models during kernel fallback.

maya: sketching config I want to try on a canary pool:

```json
{
  "allocator": {
    "workspace_headroom_pct": 10,
    "compact_threshold_secs": 5
  },
  "kv_cache": {
    "per_model_soft_quota_mb": {"gpt-med": 1024, "gpt-small": 256, "embedder": 128},
    "adaptive_credit": true,
    "credit_reduction_on_fallback_pct": 40
  },
  "routing": {
    "batch_autoscale": true,
    "max_batch_tokens": 2048
  }
}
```

sophia: can we add a profiler hook to record kernel selection and workspace high-water mark per-request? that way we can correlate kernel fallback with fragmentations.

chen: infra-bot can attach lightweight traces. @infra-bot can you add a trace tag for kernel_variant + workspace_hwm into the perf logs for the canary pool? :pray:

infra-bot: scheduled perf-trace tag addition on pool=canary-3, rollout ETA 20m. Will add fields: kernel_variant, workspace_hwm_mb, kv_evictions_at_request.

aj: quick sanity check numbers from local repro (mixed models, 2 co-resident):
- p50 token_ms: 1.9 -> 2.1 after kernel change
- p95 token_ms: 7.2 -> 9.8
- kv hitrate: 86% -> 63% under packing
- fragmentation metric (free_runs): 12 -> 34

liam: yikes on hitrate drop. that would explain cost and latency. i think buffer reuse path for attention scratch was bypassed due to kernel ABI change; need to re-enable reuse for fallback kernels or keep selection constrained for cohosted scenarios.

maya: i like two-pronged approach: (A) short-term: conservative kernel selection for multi-model tenancy (prefer kernel variants with stable scratch size); (B) medium-term: adapt allocator to be fallback-aware plus smarter kv-credit that evicts lower-priority entries preemptively instead of compacting whole slab.

chen: for (B) i prototyped an evict-scoring function that includes "expected_reuse_score" and "future_sequence_risk". if we evict low score entries before compact, fragmentation stays lower. want to run a sim.

maya: please add sim, include mixed arrival patterns and A/B on workspace_headroom 5% vs 10% vs 15%. aim to run ~100k traces.

aj: i'll hook up the traffic replay and run 3x sims on canary infra. adding param sweep for batch_autoscale on/off.

liam: can we also instrument per-model kv_prefetch timings? currently prefetch fires on route entry but may collide with compaction. measure prefetch latency and whether it increases peak memory at collision.

maya: yes. also add a metric for "swap_prefetch_overlap_compact_count" — count when prefetch window overlaps a compaction event within 200ms. that's our primary failure mode.

infra-bot: perf traces live. running sims: job ids queued [canary-sim-221, canary-sim-222, canary-sim-223]. ETA 45m.

sophia: once sims finish let's review: key outputs needed = p99 token_ms, kv_hitrate, fragmentation_runs, OOM_count, swap_prefetch_overlap_count. can you post a short summary table in thread?

maya: agreed. if we get >2x p95 or any OOMs in the canary with default kernel-selection we rollback. otherwise we push fallback-aware allocator + adaptive kv-credit to the pool and monitor for 24h.

chen: noted. i'll start the sim code and post results. rough plan timeline: sim + short fixes today, rollout canary tomorrow morning, wider rollout after 24h stability.

liam: thanks team. small follow-up: if we go with conservative kernel selection for co-residency, let's add an opt-in flag per-deployment so dedicated customers still get the faster kernels.

maya: good call. ok i'll open a PR for the config + canary run after sims. thx. :thumbsup:
